Return one score per feasible bin; higher wins and ties choose the first bin. The evaluator opens a new bin only when no existing bin fits. Minimize the number of bins used across the search instances. You cannot see future items.

Return exactly one function: def priority(item, bins):. item is the current positive integer item size; bins is a list of feasible bin residual capacities. Return a numeric list with exactly len(bins) scores, in input order; larger scores are preferred and ties use the earliest bin. The evaluator handles feasibility and opening bins. Use only numeric local assignments, if/else, return, numeric list literals, single-generator list comprehensions over bins or numeric lists, optional comprehension filters, integer list indexing, + - * / // % **, numerical comparisons, and/or/not, and conditional expressions. Permitted calls: abs, min, max, sum, len, round, sqrt, log, exp (no keywords). No imports, attributes, strings, general loops, recursion, external state, list multiplication, generators, or other calls. Do not rebind item, bins, priority, or helper names.
